title: Feds Charge 11 in Major Sex Trafficking Bust Along South L.A.'s Figueroa Corridor - NewsBreak
text: LOS ANGELES – Federal and local authorities have charged 11 members and associates of the South Los Angeles-based Hoover Criminal Gang in what officials describe as the first major takedown of a sex trafficking operation on the city’s notorious Figueroa Corridor. The 31-count indictment alleges the defendants trafficked minors and adults — including runaways and children from the foster care system — through force, fraud, or coercion, often branding victims with tattoos and recruiting them via social media. Acting United States Attorney Bill Essayli said, “The U.S. Department of Justice, under the leadership of Attorney General Pamela Bondi, is making Los Angeles safer by arresting prolific gang members who are viciously trafficking young woman and children for sex.” Six suspects, including Avery Amoako of Long Beach and Jared Evans of Los Angeles’ Mid-City area, were arrested Wednesday and are expected to appear in federal court downtown. Authorities are still searching for Bryan Isrel of South Los Angeles. According to the indictment, from February 2021 to August 2025, the gang controlled prostitution along the Figueroa Corridor. Victims were required to turn over all earnings and faced violence, public humiliation, or deprivation of food and drugs for disobedience. Investigators say members pooled resources to rent motel rooms, including the Stadium Inn in South Los Angeles, where a 14-year-old was allegedly trafficked in 2024. HSI Los Angeles Special Agent in Charge Eddy Wang stated, “No human should be for sale – not here in Los Angeles or anywhere in our society.” LAPD Chief Jim McDonnell said victims, “many of them minors, runaways, or from the foster care system – were preyed upon by individuals who sought to profit from their pain.” If convicted, several defendants face a mandatory minimum of 15 years in federal prison and could receive life sentences.
